scope.flow: POST_ONLY limit order posting against the per-side order cap in the limit order book
scope.environment: limit order book contract with _processLimitAskOrder() enforcing maxNumLimitsPerSide

statements.text: _processLimitAskOrder() enforces a hard cap on the number of active ask orders per side (maxNumLimitsPerSide).
Expired limit orders remain resident in the ask book and are not filtered or removed before the capacity check.
ds.askTree.size() counts all orders regardless of whether they are expired or actionable, and no logic removes or invalidates expired orders before the capacity check.
A trader attempts to post a competitive valid limit order.
Malicious actors occupy book space with expired orders.
Valid competitive limit orders are denied because the book is perceived as full even though resident orders are inactive or expired.
One side of the book can be frozen.
Malicious actors could selectively deny participation for specific price ranges or actors because the expiration range is not checked at order posting.
The per-side order cap should count only active, non-expired orders so that valid limit orders are not rejected due to expired orders occupying book space.

ambiguities: Report does not state who may post expired orders or whether posting is permissionless.
No explicit numeric value for maxNumLimitsPerSide or the number of expired orders needed to fill the cap.
Whether expired orders can actually be created and left resident is asserted but not shown as an observed transaction.
Order of attack steps (occupy then post) is inferred from the griefing narrative, not explicitly sequenced.
